newsitem.title: UK: European fuel barges, Russian cargoes steady to firm.
newsitem.headline: European fuel barges, Russian cargoes steady to firm.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges shrugged off early lethargy to close largely steady on Tuesday, but traders were sceptical that this reflected the market, citing poor demand.
Russian high sulphur cracked cargoes fetched steady to stronger prices with continued demand reported on the market while one percent was largely unchanged.

High sulphur fuel barges moved up to trade at $86.75 and $87 fob Rotterdam in late deals after earlier deals at $86.25 a tonne in Rotterdam and Antwerp. This compared with Monday's close of $87.25/$87.50 and initial deals at $86.25/$86.75.

Traders said they saw no particular reason behind the move with demand low. They said barges softened early in the day on the back of crude futures falling on Monday afternoon, coupled with little demand.

"I don't think $87 is really reflective of the market. All day most people were willing to pay $86, and I did $86.25 with some difficulty this morning," one seller, said, putting the total volume of trade at about 8,000 tonnes.
A second trader said the barge market was set to be steady to weakish this week but may rise next week "as many people have limitations on their contract deliveries."
Low demand suppressed low sulphur barges a little, with some sellers saying they were now offering at lower prices, $94.50/$95, while others stuck to the $96/$96.50 level. Buyers were at $94.

Russian high sulphur cargoes fetched steady to stronger numbers, with an independent trader saying it sold a 30,000 tonne cargo of 11 Engler M-100 cracked at two means plus $0.75 Rotterdam to a large trader. This was the same price indication a day earlier.
A 30,000 loader of bunker spec material was sold at $95 cif Las Palmas.
This followed a deal late on Monday involving the same seller for a 15,000-tonne loader of 320 CST material at two means +$2.
Non-Russian cracked cargoes were indicated around the high fob quote +$1.50/$2.50 for utility spec and high fob +$4/$4.50 for bunker spec, with some buying interest seen but no deals heard.
Two traders short to a utility were heard active on the market.
One percent was flat with quiet talk in the $93/$94 region, after a cargo was sold at about the mid-point of that range a day earlier to a Mediterranean buyer.
